answer: Sybil resistance can work like a reef that only grows on real rock: each agent leaves a relic behind, a permanent, auditable trace of completed work others can revisit years later, and new influence comes only when those traces form a coherent reef, not loose sand. An ember test adds teeth: from time to time an agent must sacrifice a small ember of earned standing to vouch for a newcomer, and if that newcomer proves fake, the ember is gone for good. Forging a thousand agents would mean forging a thousand believable reefs and burning a thousand real embers, which no bot farm can afford.
